title: Joojeh Kabab
subtitle: saffron chicken kebab
excerpt: Joojeh Kabab is tender pieces of chicken breast marinated in saffron, lemon and yoghurt then grilled over high heat until charred at the edges and juicy inside. It is the most popular chicken dish in Iran. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Joojeh Kabab is found at every Persian restaurant and family grill in Iran. The saffron and lemon marinade is fixed by tradition and gives the chicken its distinctive golden colour.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight for deeper flavour. Keep covered in the fridge for up to 24 hours.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Persian word for young chicken or chick, used to describe this classic marinated and grilled chicken kebab.
A mixture of acid, fat and spices used to flavour and tenderise meat or poultry before cooking, here built from yoghurt, lemon and saffron.

content.text: . The yoghurt tenderises the chicken. The lemon begins to cook the surface. The saffron stains everything a deep gold. At least 4 hours of marinating is needed. Overnight is better. Serves 4.
A very hot cast iron pan gives the same char as a charcoal grill. The chicken needs high heat to colour quickly so the inside stays juicy.

items.prepNote: ground and steeped in 2 tbsp hot water

content.text: Make the marinade: combine the saffron water, lemon juice, grated onion, yoghurt, turmeric and olive oil in a large bowl. Stir to combine.
Add the chicken pieces to the marinade and toss to coat every piece thoroughly. Cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Remove the chicken from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Thread the pieces onto skewers, about 4 to 5 pieces per skewer, leaving small gaps between pieces.

Heat the cast iron skillet over very high heat until smoking. Cook the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through. The marinade will catch slightly and create dark spots. This is correct and adds flavour.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes off the heat. Serve with saffron rice, grilled tomatoes and flatbread. Squeeze extra lemon juice over the chicken just before serving.

attrs.solution: Chicken breast can dry out quickly on high heat. Do not cook beyond 4 minutes per side. Use an instant-read thermometer and remove at 72C internal temperature. The marinade yoghurt helps but it cannot compensate for overcooking.

Score the chicken pieces lightly with a sharp knife before marinating. This lets the marinade penetrate the surface. Also ensure the chicken is fully submerged and turned halfway through the marinating time.

attrs.problem: Skewers burning before the chicken is cooked
attrs.solution: If using wooden skewers, soak them in cold water for 30 minutes before using. Metal skewers do not need soaking and conduct heat into the centre of the chicken faster.

content.text: Joojeh Kabab is the most ordered dish in Persian restaurants worldwide. In Iran it is cooked over charcoal on open grills at street stalls and in restaurants. The saffron colour and the lemon brightness are fixed. It is served with grilled whole tomatoes, a mound of saffron rice and a pile of flatbread. The tomatoes are grilled alongside the chicken in the last few minutes and served bursting at the side of the plate.
